title: Probe Tiling and Trace Ownership Checklist
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working checklist for planning compact probes ("micro-tiles") and assigning trace ownership across feature rollouts. Focus is on: metric definition hygiene, trace annotation standards for multi-tenant token serving, sampling heuristics that are tenant-aware and cost-conscious, and a small decision matrix for dashboard pruning / panel tiling.

High-level goals:
- Keep operator investigation time low by making probes small, deterministically addressable, and cheap to query.
- Ensure trace anchors are present for every probe tile so we can reconstruct sessionless or short-lived inference requests.
- Assign clear owners for traces + dashboard panels so telemetry changes during rollouts are auditable.
- Control query and trace budget: prioritize p95/p99 tail probes, Kv-cache probes, and probe tiles that historically explain >60% of incident diagnostic value.

Core concepts (new terms used here):
- probe_tile: a compact probe unit (usually 1–3 metrics + 1 synthetic span anchor) focused on a single hypothesis (e.g., cold-KV-eviction, prefix-warmth). probe_tile_id is the deterministic id used for sampling keys.
- trace_anchor: a small span emitted synchronously with the request that contains minimal routing metadata to stitch longer traces later.
- tenant-weighted sampling: sample more traces from tenants that represent more SLO risk (high quota usage or high spend) while keeping global query budget.

Metric definitions (recommendation template):
- prefix_warmth_index: ratio( requests_with_prefix_in_kv_cache / requests_total ) aggregated by minute, tag by model.version, route, and probe_tile_id. Unit: fraction (0..1). Alert: monotonic drop >25% over 5m for top-5 tenants.
- kv_cache_hit_rate_adjusted: cached_hits / (cached_hits + cache_misses + eps) where cached_hits counts only hits shorter than 200ms to avoid counting noisy warms. Tag: model_variant, tenant_weight_bucket.
- probe_micro_latency_ms_p95: p95 latency of a probe tile's synthetic request path (includes network + runtime). Use histogram with explicit buckets.
- probe_tile_eviction_score: heuristic score combining kv_cache_evictions_per_min and tenant_request_rate; used to rank probe tiles for prioritization.

Trace instrumentation guidelines (must-haves for every probe):
- Minimal synchronous span (trace_anchor) must include: trace_id, probe_tile_id, model.version, model.variant, route, node_id (shard), request_tier, tenant_id_hash (sha256:8), kv_probe_flag (true|false).
- For privacy: tenant_id must always be hashed and salted; do not include raw PII in any span or attribute.
- Correlation: ensure trace_anchor links to client_correlation_id (if provided) and to session_id when present.
- Span naming: use short canonical names: anchor.probe_tile, op.kv_check, op.kv_lookup. Avoid freeform names.

Sampling heuristics (practical algorithm):
- Global trace_budget_per_min = 2000 anchors/min (adjusted by capacity).
- Tiered deterministic sampling: if tenant_weight_bucket == high -> sample_rate = 10% for that tenant; medium -> 2%; low -> 0.2%. Deterministic rule: hash(tenant_id_hash || probe_tile_id) % 10000 < (sample_rate*100). This ensures even coverage across tiles and reproducible samples.
- Adaptive tail sampling override: if probe_micro_latency_ms_p95 > threshold for a tile, enable 100% sampling for that tile for 10 minutes (cooldown 30m).
- Sessionless requests: use response-size-based sampling (larger outputs are more diagnostic). For response_length > 512 tokens, bump sample rate *2.

Dashboard / panel tiling decision matrix (compact):
- For each panel, evaluate: cost_per_query (approx seconds*cost), diagnostic_value (subjective 1..5), owner, query_frequency.
- Keep if diagnostic_value >=3 AND cost_per_query <= budget_per_panel (default budget_per_panel = 0.5s-equivalent).
- Consolidate panels if they share >70% of underlying queries (merge into a tile with drilldown links).
- Deprecate panels with diagnostic_value <=2 for 90 days and low usage. Move to 'archive' tier with weekly sampling dashboards.

Operational checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Define probe_tile_id and add to probe catalog (confluence:OBS-PROBE-PLANS-412).
- [ ] Add trace_anchor annotation schema to telemetry spec and ship instrumentation PR (see linked PR).
- [ ] Write dashboard tile with 3 panels max: heatmap (kv warmth), latency histogram, tenant top-N. Keep queries under 100ms if possible.
- [ ] Assign owner for probe_tile (owner + 1 backup). Document owner in panel description.
- [ ] Allocate sampling budget and update sampling config (ConfigMap: telemetry/sampling).
- [ ] Smoke test: generate synthetic traffic for cold/warm paths and validate trace linkage within 5m.

Oncall playbook snippets:
- If kv_cache_hit_rate_adjusted drops for a tenant: check probe_tile_eviction_score and latency p95 for the tile. If eviction_score > threshold -> escalate to serving-runtime oncall.
- Use trace_anchor to jump to node-level spans; if anchor missing in >10% of sampled requests, fail the rollout and disable.

Dashboard layout suggestions (operator UX):
- Top row: global KPI tiles (global kv_cache_hit_rate_adjusted, global prefix_warmth_index p50/p95).
- Middle row: per-probe_tile microdash (select drop-down of tile IDs), low-cardinality by tenant_weight_bucket.
- Bottom row: incident correlators (request_rate anomalies, recent trace anchors with latency overlays).
- Drilldown link from any tile directly to a limited trace viewer filter by probe_tile_id and tenant_id_hash.

Cost control knobs (practical defaults):
- Query budget per dashboard: 1000 queries/day for a single-person dashboard; scale up if diagnosed value warrants.
- Trace retention tiers: anchors retained 7d full, heavy traces (post-join) retained 30d for high-paying tenants only.

Ownership and governance:
- Owner responsibilities: maintain probe_tile definition, own dashboard panels, validate sampling config during rollouts, run postmortem when probes fail.
- Quarterly audit: telemetry steward will run a probe catalog audit for stale tiles and orphan panels.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Should we store probe_tile definitions alongside code (repo telemetry/probes.yaml) or in Confluence only? (Pros: CI checks; Cons: extra release coupling) -> Owner: Ruth.
- Q2: How to handle cross-tenant correlated events without ever exposing tenant ids in traces? Prototype: maintain a correlation table of hashed tenant cohorts that is access-controlled. -> Owner: Priya.
- TODO: Add example SQL for computing prefix_warmth_index in the metrics warehouse and a sample Grafana query. -> Owner: Samir.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the probe_tile_id namespace short (e.g., kvc:v1:tile_03). Avoid long human-readable names in code.
- Strive for deterministic sampling to make A/B comparisons reproducible.
- Tie expensive dashboards to feature flags so we can turn off panels when experimenting with new quantized models.

References and useful links:
- Confluence: OBS-PROBE-PLANS-412 (probe catalog)
- Jira: OBS-823 (sampling config rollout)
- GitHub: telemetry instrumentation PR #217

Last notes: this doc is intentionally compact — keep probe tiles small and stable. The next step after agreement here is to prototype one probe tile for a known cold-cache regression and run a 2-week experiment to validate sampling and downstream cost impact.

-- Jordan
